Exercise 4: Enablement Decisions

28 points
Choose the best approach for each real-world sales enablement challenge.
Scenario 1 7 points

Marcus messages at 4:47 PM: "Going against Competitor X tomorrow. Battlecard is from Q3. What's new?" You have a meeting in 15 minutes. What's the best long-term solution?

Stay late and manually compile a brief for Marcus
Point Marcus to the existing battlecard since it's mostly still accurate
Build a RAG-powered system where Marcus can query current competitive intel in natural language
Hire more PMMs to handle real-time competitive requests
Scenario 2 7 points

Your VP asks how you'll prove PMM enablement value now that sales reps can generate their own competitive summaries with ChatGPT. What's the best response?

Create more battlecards faster to stay ahead of what reps can generate
Block sales from using their own AI tools
Shift measurement to win rates in competitive deals where PMM-curated intelligence was used vs not
Focus on producing higher quality PDFs with better design
Scenario 3 7 points

You're starting to build an agent-powered enablement system. You track 8 competitors. What's the recommended first step?

Build monitoring for all 8 competitors simultaneously
Pick your #1 competitor and build the full pipeline — monitor, RAG, interface — then expand
Wait until you have a dedicated AI engineering team to help
Start with the competitor that has the least information available
Scenario 4 7 points

A sales rep says: "I asked ChatGPT about Competitor X and it gave me good talking points. Why do I need PMM?" What's the enablement paradox insight?

ChatGPT isn't reliable enough for sales conversations
ChatGPT can generate competent content, but PMM provides the strategic intelligence that makes content accurate and differentiated
Reps should never use ChatGPT for competitive prep
PMM needs to produce content faster than ChatGPT
